newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: At least 15 killed in Sri Lanka fighting.
newsitem.headline: At least 15 killed in Sri Lanka fighting.

text.p: Several Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels and four soldiers were killed in a skirmish in Sri Lanka's northeast, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.
It said in a statement that troops in the northeastern Nedunkeni town, which the army captured in May, were confronted by rebels late on Tuesday.
"Troops retaliated, causing casualties among the terrorists," the statement said.
It said four soldiers were wounded in the fighting and troops recovered four rebel bodies along with their weapons.

The statement said the rebels had fired mortars at the military's forward positions near Omanthai, north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, late on Tuesday. Troops retaliated with artillery fire, it said.
Vavuniya lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the cpaital Colombo.
Military officials in the north said seven soldiers were killed in a mine blast in the northern Jaffna peninsula early on Wednesday. One was wounded.
A spokesman for LTTE in London was no immediately available for comment.
Sri Lankan troops are battling the LTTE in the island's north in an attempt to open a crucial highway linking the northern Jaffna peninsula with the rest of the island.

Troops captured key rebel towns in the offensive launched in May, but the operation slowed down after the LTTE, who are fighting for an independent homeland for the minority Tamil population in Sri Lanka's north and east, launched two fierce counter-attacks last month.
Scores of guerrillas and soldiers were killed in the fighting.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
